items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the transportation law, in relation to requiring the
department of transportation to annually prepare and submit to the legislature
certain highway pavement and bridge condition reports
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S199

SPONSOR: KAPLAN
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the transportation law, in relation to requiring the
department of transportation to annually prepare and submit to the
legislature certain highway pavement and bridge condition reports

 
PURPOSE:

This legislation requires an annual report highway pavement and bridge
report be submitted to the Legislature.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

§ 1- Amends section 14 of the transportation law by adding subdivision
36, which requires a report be made regarding highway and bridge condi-
tions, capital letting and implementation, capital program accomplish-
ments, and non MTA downstate suburban and upstate transit capital
programs to be distributed by the governor.

Subdivision a of section 36 sets that the fiscal report for the upcoming
year shall be published on June 1 each year, beginning on June 1, 2021.
Included in this report also are funds pursuant to New York Works.This
would include projects expected to be advertised for public bid in the
respective fiscal year, project descriptions, proposed month of letting,
project identification number, and project cost estimates.

Subdivision b of section 36 sets that also on June 1 of each year,
beginning on June 1, 2021, an accomplishment report for the prior fiscal
year will be published detailing the amount of funding obligated for
major capital programs and the detailing of which programs are included
in that.  Subdivision c of section 36 sets that a highway pavement and
bridge condition report, and the provisions that would be included in
that report, shall be published on June 1 of every year, beginning on
June 1, 2020.

Subdivision d of section 36 sets that a report shall be published
detailing the allocation and disbursement of the funds that were
provided for the prior state fiscal year, and the provisions therein,
every year on June 1, beginning on June 1, 2021.

§ 2- Effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

This legislation seeks to help inform the Legislature and public as to
where funds are needed and are being appropriated to help repair and
maintain New York's roads and bridges. A similar concept was included as
part of the DOT 2015-2019 five year capital plan, this legislation seeks
to codify into transportation law this report. Having this information
readily available will help pinpoint and address the roads and bridges
that are in need of repair, while ensuring that the public can feel
certain that the highways and bridges they use are being addressed to
the best capabilities of New York.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:  S. 7885A/A. 10090A: Passed Senate in 2020

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
